title: Microsoft offers mass buyouts for roughly a quarter of its workforce
titleZh: Microsoft offers mass buyouts for roughly a quarter of its workforce
author: doctorzook
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: AbbeFaria
comments.textRawHtml:
Ex-MSFT here. I resigned in June, I was an L63. I spent 8 years at MSFT across two stints.

My last 18 months at MSFT were deeply unproductive. Constant reorgs, the work not being aligned to my capabilities and unfortunately just the general feeling that I was under worked and had very little opportunity for career advancement.

I would look at my colleagues and sister teams and wonder, why do they need these many people to work on something so trivial ? Or how did this person get promoted for doing that work ? I am sure envy played a part in the second question but it was legitimate. Remember, all this was before LLM tools were prevalent.

In the end, I left off my own volition. In my last 6 months, I did very little work, if at all any. I thought why am I being paid so handsomely for such little and trivial work. I did try interviewing in a few different teams but didn’t make it (Azure Files and Hyperscale DB). If I had stayed, I would have been swiftly laid off or if I was lucky enough last long till this buyout.

I think same is true for all Big Tech companies. Too many employees doing not enough or quality work.
comments.textZhHtml:
前 MSFT 在此。我六月份辞职了，我是L63。我在 MSFT 工作了 8 年，期间曾两次任职。

我在 MSFT 的最后 18 个月毫无成效。不断的重组，工作与我的能力不符，不幸的是，我普遍感觉自己工作不足，职业发展的机会很少。

我会看着我的同事和姐妹团队，想知道，为什么他们需要这么多人来处理如此琐碎的事情？或者这个人是如何因从事这项工作而获得晋升的？我确信嫉妒在第二个问题中发挥了作用，但这是合理的。请记住，这一切都是在 LLM 工具盛行之前发生的。

最终，我放弃了自己的意愿。在过去的六个月里，我几乎没有做任何工作（如果有的话）。 我想为什么我做这么琐碎的工作却能得到如此丰厚的报酬。我确实尝试过面试几个不同的团队，但没有成功（Azure 文件和超大规模数据库）。如果我留下来，我会很快被解雇，或者如果我足够幸运，能坚持很长时间直到这次收购。

我认为所有大型科技公司都是如此。太多员工的工作质量不够。

children.author: nomel
children.textRawHtml:
The big tech companies are getting old. I think it's a fundamental rule that the competence and effectiveness of an org must fall, over time, driven by the fact that a person will more readily hire someone they can understand than someone that is more intelligent/competent/effective. This causes a slow degradation.

I also think there's been a drastic shift in the working culture of tech/engineering spaces, in general, over the last 15 years. From my experience, it's definitely drifted away from a bunch of nerds solving problems to something more towards emotional/personal/politics. I recently saw someone cry when a person very kindly asked them to explain a discrepancy. "Back in my day" people would just state facts, point out flaws, and argue a bit, and have fun doing it, for better or worse.
children.textZhHtml:
大型科技公司正在变老。我认为这是一条基本规则，随着时间的推移，一个组织的能力和有效性必定会下降，这是因为一个人更愿意雇佣他们能够理解的人，而不是更聪明/更有能力/更高效的人。这会导致缓慢的退化。

我还认为，在过去 15 年里，技术/工程领域的工作文化总体上发生了巨大转变。根据我的经验，它肯定已经从一群解决问题的书呆子转向了更注重情感/个人/政治的东西。最近，当一个人非常友善要求他们解释差异时，我看到有人哭了。 “在我那个时代”，人们只会陈述事实，指出缺陷，争论一下，并乐在其中，无论好坏。

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml:
Maybe I'm just lucky but I have a few gen Z coworkers and they are probably more often than not the voice of reason in our org (start up with 8 engineers). I think if an employee can't handle simple constructive criticism or clarifications maybe they should not be employed.

I did used to work for a consulting firm about a decade ago, and I was leading a staff augmentation project with another company and I was once chastised for saying "hey guys" in a chat because there were women in the group. I was encouraged to use "y'all" but not wanting to sound like I was from the south, I just used "peeps" which was somehow okay.

I'm all for inclusive language but I thought that was a bridge too far.
children.textZhHtml:
也许我只是幸运，但我有一些 Z 世代同事，他们可能经常是我们组织中理性的声音（从 8 名工程师开始）。我认为，如果员工无法处理简单的建设性批评或澄清，也许他们不应该被雇用。

大约十年前，我曾在一家咨询公司工作过，当时我正在与另一家公司领导一个员工扩充项目，我曾经因为在聊天中说“嘿，伙计们”而受到惩罚，因为小组中有女性。我被鼓励使用“y'all”，但不想听起来像我来自南方，我只是使用“peeps”，这在某种程度上还可以。

我完全支持包容性语言，但我认为这是一座太过遥远的桥梁。

children.author: throwaway20222
children.textRawHtml:
A coworker was asked in a meeting how he was holding up after pulling an epic two day sprint to deliver a project that saved our butts. He replied “I felt like jumping out of a window.”

Someone reported him for not warning the room about suicidal ideation before saying it and not considering that it might be triggering. He was actually reprimanded.

Unfortunately typical of the place. I left soon after.
children.textZhHtml:
一位同事在一次会议上被问到，在完成了为期两天的史诗级冲刺以交付一个拯救了我们的项目后，他的表现如何。他回答说：“我想跳出窗外。”

有人举报他在说出自杀意念之前没有警告房间里的人，也没有考虑到这可能会触发。他实际上受到了谴责。

不幸的是，这是这个地方的典型现象。不久我就离开了。

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml: That's wild! I wonder how far I could get at a place like that by saying random things trigger me, like "don't call it a sprint because I once tripped and broke a tooth while sprinting" or something like that. Make an entire organization change their jargon and use fun words like "this is our two week adventure!"
children.textZhHtml: 太疯狂了！我想知道如果我说一些随机的事情触发我，我能在这样的地方走多远，比如“不要称之为冲刺，因为我曾经在冲刺时绊倒并摔断了一颗牙齿”或类似的话。让整个组织改变他们的行话并使用有趣的词语，例如“这是我们为期两周的冒险！”

children.author: sa48k
children.textRawHtml: I once told someone that they shouldn't use 'flesh out an idea' because it's offensive to skeletons.
children.textZhHtml: 我曾经告诉过某人，他们不应该使用“充实一个想法”，因为这会冒犯骷髅。

children.author: walthamstow
children.textRawHtml: In a previous job, in whiteboard sessions, one of the team would always refer to something as the "final solution" and I could never tell whether he was doing it on purpose or not
children.textZhHtml: 在之前的工作中，在白板会议中，团队中的一个人总是将某些内容称为“最终解决方案”，而我永远无法判断他是否是故意这样做的

children.author: eastbound
children.textRawHtml: That may be the game that others are playing. I always wonder how much of this is other countries paying agents to spoil the productivity of the West, as a retaliation for unmerited wars we do to them.

This whole language purity test, whether from the left or right, is just a load of performative bollocks.
